rics.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score 620-659
rics.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 620-659 — subprime band. NY Fed Household Debt and Credit Report quarterly. Sensitive to lending-standard shifts.
rics.how_to_use: Volumes rise when banks ease standards (cycle peaks) and collapse in tightening cycles. As a share of total originations, this band fell from 15-20% pre-2008 to 5-8% post-Dodd-Frank — a structural shift toward higher-quality lending.

rics.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score 660-719
rics.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 660-719 — near-prime/middle band. The pre-2008 mainstream borrower segment, now a smaller share given migration toward higher scores post-crisis.
rics.how_to_use: Watch share vs prime (720-759) as a cycle indicator: rising near-prime share indicates lender willingness to extend credit further. Falling share signals tightening — a leading indicator of housing slowdowns.

rics.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score 720-759
rics.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 720-759 — prime band. Largest single share of originations historically. Standard conforming-loan borrower.
rics.how_to_use: Most stable band through cycles. Fell ~70% from 2021 peak as rate hikes killed refinance volumes. Use as the 'baseline mortgage market' gauge — purchase originations in this band track home-sales volume.

rics.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score <620
rics.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score below 620 — deep subprime band. Very small post-2008 (banks largely don't lend here; FHA dominates this credit-quality segment).
rics.how_to_use: Monitor for any uptick as a sign of loosening credit standards. Pre-2008, this band exceeded $50B/quarter. Post-Dodd-Frank QM rules effectively shut down deep-subprime conventional lending; FHA fills the gap with explicit federal guarantee.

rics.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score >760
rics.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 760+ — super-prime band. Largest dollar volume share (highest credit-quality borrowers tend to take larger loans for higher-priced homes).
rics.how_to_use: The 'jumbo + prime conforming' segment. Most resilient to rate shocks because these borrowers have alternatives (cash, equity). Useful for tracking high-end housing demand separately from broader market.

rics.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score Zero
rics.meaning: Mortgage originations with zero risk score — borrowers who lack credit-bureau histories (typically immigrants, young first-time buyers). Niche segment.
rics.how_to_use: Very small share. Useful only for tracking unusual lending patterns. Major spike would indicate credit-extension to non-traditional borrowers (concerning) — currently flat.

rics.meaning: Total mortgage originations — sum of all credit-quality bands. NY Fed quarterly Household Debt and Credit Report. Includes both purchase and refinance originations.
rics.how_to_use: Headline mortgage finance volume. Collapsed from ~$1.2T quarterly peak in 2021 to ~$400B in 2023-24 as rate hikes killed refinance demand. Track purchase-origination share separately for housing-market signal.

rics.meaning: Total student loans outstanding (memo to consumer credit) — ~$1.7T. Mostly federal direct loans; private student loans <$150B. Cumulative balance reflecting decades of borrowing minus repayments.
rics.how_to_use: Major household balance sheet item. Repayment obligations resumed Oct 2023 after pandemic forbearance; consumption headwind for borrowers. Forgiveness programs (PSLF, IDR) periodically reduce balances; track flow vs stock for cleaner signal.

rics.meaning: Total consumer credit MoM% change, annualized — Fed G.19 high-frequency credit-growth signal. Captures revolving (cards) + nonrevolving (auto + student + personal) flows.
rics.how_to_use: Watch for sharp decelerations as consumer-stress signal. 2008 crisis saw -5% annualized; 2020 COVID saw -10% (credit-card payoffs from stimulus). Revolving accelerating + nonrevolving decelerating = households leaning on cards (late-cycle stress).

rics.meaning: Consumer credit, monthly absolute change — net credit creation flow. Fed G.19 release ~5th business day of each month, two-month lag.
rics.how_to_use: Decompose into revolving (cards) and nonrevolving (auto/student) for cleaner signal. Auto loan flows track auto sales; revolving flows show whether households are running balances or paying down. Stress shows up in revolving first.

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at depository institutions — banks' auto loan + personal loan book (excludes mortgages, excludes credit cards). About half of all bank consumer lending by stock.
rics.how_to_use: Compare to total nonrevolving (G.19) for bank vs nonbank share. Auto loan share of bank lending has fallen as captive finance (GM Financial, Ford Credit, Toyota Financial) gained share — a structural shift in auto financing.

rics.meaning: Consumer credit at depository institutions, flows — net new bank consumer credit creation per period. Bank-channel credit-creation flow.
rics.how_to_use: Decompose vs nonbank flows (credit unions, finance companies) to see channel mix. Banks are ~50% of consumer credit; share has been falling as fintechs and captive auto finance grow.

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, flows — auto + student + personal loan flows. Excludes credit cards (revolving).
rics.how_to_use: Auto loans dominate (~60% of nonrevolving flows). Student loans flat post-2020 forbearance/forgiveness. Track auto-loan flows for auto-sales pulse — they correlate ~0.8.

rics.description: Consumer credit - Actual, Absolute change, USD
rics.meaning: Consumer credit, absolute change in USD — total monthly net change in outstanding consumer credit. Same as aUSCRDTLAB at different release.
rics.how_to_use: Watch for sharp decelerations as consumer-stress signal. 2008 crisis saw monthly contractions of $20-30B; 2020 COVID saw similar drops driven by credit-card paydowns from stimulus.

rics.description: Consumer credit memo, motor vehicle loans
rics.meaning: Motor vehicle loans (memo item).
rics.how_to_use: ~$1.6T outstanding. Rate-sensitive; new vs used split matters for credit risk.

rics.description: Consumer credit memo, motor vehicle loans, flows
rics.meaning: Consumer credit memo: motor vehicle loans, flows — net new auto-loan creation per period. Tracks auto-finance volume.
rics.how_to_use: Correlates with auto sales (~0.8). Track auto-loan-flow growth vs sales growth: when loans grow faster than sales, average loan-to-value rising (subprime expansion); when slower, customers paying cash.

rics.meaning: Consumer credit outstanding (alternate framing) — same conceptual measure as aUSCRDOUTA. Total household nonmortgage debt.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check vs aUSCRDOUTA. Total ~$5T as of 2024 (revolving ~$1.3T, nonrevolving ~$3.7T). Track YoY growth rate as consumer-leverage signal.

rics.meaning: Consumer Credit Outstanding total — Federal Reserve G.19 monthly. Credit cards + auto + student + personal. ~$5T total.
rics.how_to_use: Watch growth rate alongside delinquencies (aUSBDLCOCQ/A) to gauge consumer balance-sheet stress. Composition: revolving (cards) + non-revolving (auto, student, personal). Excludes mortgage debt.

rics.meaning: Consumer credit outstanding, net change (annualized rate) — annualized version of monthly absolute change. Smoothed credit-creation pace.
rics.how_to_use: Annualized rate makes monthly volatility comparable to year-over-year stock change. Useful for comparing fast-growing vs slow-growing periods. Pre-COVID norm ~5%/year; post-COVID swings have been much larger.

rics.meaning: Credit unions consumer credit.
rics.how_to_use: Credit unions ~12% of consumer credit. Member-owned, often cheaper rates.

rics.meaning: Consumer credit at credit unions, flows — net new credit-union consumer credit creation. Credit unions are ~12% of consumer credit market.
rics.how_to_use: Credit unions tend to lend to higher-credit-quality borrowers and have lower charge-off rates. Growing share post-2008 (banks tightened, CUs filled gap). Track for member-base growth and lending standards.

rics.meaning: Finance companies consumer credit.
rics.how_to_use: Captive finance arms (Ford Motor Credit, GM Financial). Auto-heavy.

rics.meaning: Consumer credit, finance companies, flows — net new credit creation by finance companies (Ford Motor Credit, GM Financial, Toyota Financial, etc.).
rics.how_to_use: Captive auto finance dominates this category. Flows correlate with auto sales but with higher beta because captives often offer subsidized financing to support sales.

rics.meaning: Total consumer credit flows — net new credit creation across all channels (banks, credit unions, finance companies, nonfinancial business, federal government).
rics.how_to_use: Aggregate flow measure. Decompose by channel for source of growth. Federal government student loans are a major share post-2010. Falling flows = consumer-credit cycle turning.

rics.meaning: Consumer credit, nonfinancial business — credit extended directly by retailers (store credit cards, layaway, etc.). Smaller channel.
rics.how_to_use: Niche category but cyclical. Retailer-direct credit grew during pandemic for buy-now-pay-later programs. Track for retailer-credit-program expansion.

rics.meaning: Consumer credit, nonfinancial business, flows — net new credit creation by retailers/nonfinancial businesses.
rics.how_to_use: Track for BNPL (buy-now-pay-later) ecosystem growth. Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay programs partially captured here. Volatile due to small base.

rics.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving credit unions, flows
rics.meaning: Consumer credit, nonrevolving at credit unions, flows — net new credit-union nonrevolving (auto + personal) lending.
rics.how_to_use: CUs growing share post-2008. Watch for member-base growth and lending standards. Auto lending is dominant within CU nonrevolving.

rics.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving depository institutions, flows
rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at depository institutions, flows — net new bank nonrevolving (auto + personal) lending.
rics.how_to_use: Bank-share gauge for nonrevolving lending. Bank share has fallen as captive finance grew (auto OEMs offer subsidized rates). Watch for share recovery if captives retreat.

rics.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving federal government & Sallie Mae, flows
rics.meaning: Federal government & Sallie Mae, nonrevolving credit, flows.
rics.how_to_use: Federal student loan flow. Large negative flows during pause years.

rics.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving finance companies, flows
rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, finance companies, flows — net new finance-company nonrevolving lending. Mostly auto captives.
rics.how_to_use: Auto-loan flow proxy. Highly sensitive to auto-sales pace. Captives use 0% promo financing to drive volume — watch promo-financing share for auto-incentive cycle.

rics.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving nonfinancial business, flows
rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, nonfinancial business, flows — retailer-direct nonrevolving lending. Smaller niche.
rics.how_to_use: Track for installment-credit programs. BNPL ecosystem partially flows here. Volatile due to small base.

rics.description: Consumer credit, terms of credit - comm bks interest, credit card, all account
rics.meaning: Credit Card APR at commercial banks, all accounts (G.19 quarterly). ~22% in 2024 — record high.
rics.how_to_use: Spread to fed funds widened sharply post-COVID (banks raised more than rate hikes warranted). Average APR for accounts ASSESSED interest (those carrying a balance) is even higher (~24%).

rics.meaning: Non-revolving consumer credit — auto + student + personal loans. Larger than revolving; student loans dominate.
rics.how_to_use: Auto charge-offs spiking (subprime auto stress). Student loans frozen during pandemic; payments resumed October 2023. PSLF/IDR program shifts move totals around.

rics.meaning: Revolving consumer credit (credit cards). Hit ~$1.2T+ in 2024 — a record high.
rics.how_to_use: Watch nominal growth rate (~8%/yr trend, faster recently). 90+ delinquency rate (aUSBDLCOCQ/A) is now elevated, especially subprime card. Card APR (aUSCRCDACR) at ~22% is record high.

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, monthly percent change (annualized) — pace of nonrevolving (auto + student) credit growth.
rics.how_to_use: Smoother than revolving (cards). Auto-loan-driven cyclically; student-loan flows depend on policy (forgiveness, forbearance). Recent: weakened with auto-sales pullback.

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, monthly absolute change — net new nonrevolving lending per month.
rics.how_to_use: Decompose vs revolving for cycle signal. Nonrevolving cycle lags consumer-spending cycle by 1-2 months (loans booked after purchase decisions).

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit outstanding — total stock of nonrevolving credit (auto + student + personal). ~$3.7T.
rics.how_to_use: Largest share of consumer credit (~75%). Student loans alone are ~$1.7T. Watch alongside revolving (cards) outstanding for total-leverage picture.

rics.description: Nonrevolving consumer credit at credit unions
rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at credit unions — CU nonrevolving lending stock. ~$400B.
rics.how_to_use: Auto-loan-heavy. CUs gaining share post-2008. Track for member-base growth and average loan size.

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at finance companies — captive auto finance + personal-loan finance companies. ~$700B.
rics.how_to_use: Auto OEM captives dominate. Watch for share trends vs banks; captives gain share when promotional financing aggressive.

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, total flows — aggregate of all-channel nonrevolving lending creation.
rics.how_to_use: Sum of bank + CU + finance company + nonfin business + federal government nonrevolving flows. Federal government (student loans) is variable based on policy.

rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, nonfinancial business — retailer-direct installment credit stock.
rics.how_to_use: Niche category. Includes retailer financing programs and BNPL providers. Track for ecosystem growth.

rics.description: Nonrevolving consumer credit, pool of securitized assets
rics.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, pool of securitized assets — auto-loan ABS and other consumer-credit-backed securities.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks securitized funding of consumer credit. ABS issuance is the supply side; investor demand drives pricing of subprime auto deals. Watch for ABS-spread changes as credit-cycle indicator.

rics.meaning: Financial obligations ratio (FOR).
rics.how_to_use: Broader than DSR — includes rent, auto leases, property tax, insurance. Better gauge for renters.

rics.meaning: Household debt service ratio (DSR) — debt payments / disposable income.
rics.how_to_use: Master household-leverage gauge. ~10% currently — well below 2008 peak (~13%).
